newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Office Depot busy after decision.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Office Depot busy after decision.

text.p: Options on shares of Office Depot Inc drew heavy interest Tuesday after a U.S. judge late Monday granted the U.S. government a preliminary injunction halting the company's planned $4 billion merger with Staples Inc.
The news knocked shares of Office Depot sharply lower. In afternoon trading they were down 3-15/16 at 15-1/2 on consolidated volume of 21.6 million shares.
Staples gained 1-1/8 to 24-3/8 on 13.5 million shares.
Office Depot options activity was centered on the call side as investors mainly exited positions, traders said.
Activity was led by the July 20 call, July 15 call and July 17-1/2 call. Those options traded about 42,360 contracts, 34,000 contracts and 21,000 contracts, respectively.
The July 20 call, which had open interest of more than 80,000 contracts, fell 2-5/16 to 1/16.
The July 15 call, which had open interest of 51,289, dropped 4-5/16 to 15/16.
The July 17-1/2 call had open interest of nearly 62,000 contracts. It lost 3-7/16 to 3/16.
"People are trying to get out of those before they go to zero," one trader said of those Office Depot calls.
Among Office Depot puts, the July 17-1/2 traded 17,360 contracts and the July 12-1/2 traded about 12,000.
One options dealer said some of his clients had sold some Office Depot puts recently but had not returned Tuesday to buy them back.
He explained the puts were low-priced when the investors sold them and did not move that much despite the stock's action.
The July 17-1/2 put rose 3/8 to 2-1/8 and the 12-1/2 slipped 1/8 to 1/16.
Among Staples options, the July 20 calls were most active, with volume of more than 2,200 contracts. The most active put was the July 22-1/2, with turnover of about 525.
Office Depot's chief executive officer said Tuesday the company would not likely fight the court ruling against the merger.
After the ruling Monday, Staples' president said the company would likely end any attempt to merge with Office Depot.
Traders and analysts agreed that the two companies would most likely end their merger plans, which had been in the works for 10 months.
The Federal Trade Commission had oppposed the merger, contending it would raise prices.
